subject: Re: ACME - Buying process & exceptions (discount / SLA / security)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.col e@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: ACME - buying process & exceptions (discount / SLA / security)

Team — quick recap from this morning's discovery with ACME (Liam + Nina + Sanjay on parts):

Key takeaways:
- Economic buyer: Nina Patel (VP Product) — primary budget sign-off.
- Procurement timeline: procurement wants a PO by 2026-05-20 to hit June go-live.
- Security: Sanjay Rao (CISO) will run DPA + security questionnaire review; they asked for an initial DPA redline + answers to the attached security Qs.
- Decision criteria: latency SLA (p95 token latency), predictable per-token cost, and audit logging for requests.

Customer asks / exceptions they've requested:
1) One-time commercial: 25% off list for first 12 months (they asked for 25%).
2) SLA change: they want guaranteed 99.9% uptime and reduced termination notice (30 days). Our standard is 99.95% and 90-day termination notice in enterprise T&Cs.
3) Data residency: they want clarifications; their procurement is pushing for EU-resident logs (ACME has EU offices).

Asks from me to the group (please reply with approvals or notes by EOD 2026-05-13):
- Aditya: confirm whether we can authorize a commercial exception up to 20% or if we need manager approval for 25%. Provide margin impact (I put deal_id RDW-ACME-2026-0421 in HS).
- Stephanie: legal: initial read on SLA/termination request + DPA timeline. I attached the DPA draft and ACME's filled security Qs (acme_security_qs.pdf).
- Vivek: can your team support the audit logging/residency ask without infra changes? Any blockers for June go-live?
- Evelyn: if we get approval for 20% (or 25%), can you prepare the procurement checklist / PO template and confirm billing lead times?

Attachments: acme_security_qs.pdf (filled by ACME), pricing-MAX-commit.xlsx (internal parity sheet).

TL;DR: ACME is preferring a quick timeline (PO by 05/20). They requested 25% and termination/ SLA changes. Need internal approvals before I commit anything externally.

Thanks —
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - buying process & exceptions (discount / SLA / security)

Marissa — thanks for the clear summary. A few quick responses: 

- Commercial exception: I can approve up to 20% off list at my level for a first-year promotional concession, subject to a revenue commit (12 months) and pre-paid or monthly with payment guarantees. Anything >20% needs the sales manager and finance sign-off.
- SLA / termination: those are legal items. From a commercial perspective, 99.9% vs 99.95% materially increases our risk exposure; prefer to keep standard SLA and offer a capped service credit (we can negotiate credit %).
- Please confirm expected ACME ARR/first-year revenue so I can run model — I don't have the final numbers in HS yet. If they're asking 25%, we should ask for a stronger commit (usage minimum or longer term).

I'll mark deal RDW-ACME-2026-0421 for pricing exception review and loop in my manager if Marissa thinks they will hold at 25%.

-Aditya
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.col e@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 12:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME - buying process & exceptions (discount / SLA / security)

Quick legal read:
- SLA: 99.95% is our standard for Dedicated/Private; we can consider 99.9% only with compensating controls (increased credits capping liability) and explicit operational runbook commitments. We should not move to a shorter termination notice without risk assessment.
- Termination notice: 30 days introduces commercial and operational risk; if procurement insists, propose a pilot clause (30-day termination during pilot only) and 90-day thereafter.
- DPA / security: I reviewed the DPA draft attached. I'll upload an initial redline (redwood-DPA-draft.docx) and send it back to ACME legal. Sanjay's ask re: EU logs is a data residency point — we can offer region-tagged audit logs for EU regions but need Security/Infra confirmation.

Next steps: I will: (1) provide DPA redline by 2026-05-14, (2) propose SLA credit language for 99.9% vs 99.95% by 2026-05-14. Finance must sign off on any negotiated credit %s.

If procurement pushes 25% discount, we need Finance approval and a defined commitment (either ARR target or term length).

- Stephanie
Sr. Counsel | Redwood Inference
stephanie@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-DPA-draft.docx
